Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:155: And the matter of the heretic (apikoros) — our Sages, of blessed memory, explained that it refers to a man who does not conduct himself with reverence and honor toward Torah scholars, even though he does not actually demean them — such as one who demeans his fellow in front of a Torah scholar, and gives no honor to the scholar's Torah. For since the Torah is not honored in his eyes so as to conduct himself toward it with respect, he has no share in the World to Come, for this too is counted among those who desecrate the Torah. Therefore our Sages of blessed memory said (Pesachim 22b): "You shall fear the Lord your God" (Deuteronomy 6:13) — this includes Torah scholars.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:156: And the second reason: reverence for them is a cause for the fear of Heaven, for since their words are heeded because of the reverence shown them, they teach and guide the people to fear the honored and awesome Name; and it is said (I Samuel 12:18), "and all the people greatly feared the Lord and Samuel." And likewise included among heretics is one who says, What have those who study gained by their study? Is there anything he could point to and say, See, this is new — they never before permitted us to eat every raven, nor forbade us the young of doves [i.e., mocking the value of halachic study]. And such people neither know nor have heard, nor have their ears been opened to the benefits found in the occupation with Torah; and because of this, the occupation with Torah is lowly in their eyes, and they have rebelled against the light of its virtue, and they have no share in the World to Come. Therefore we have been obligated to teach the children of Judah the benefits found in the occupation with Torah, and we have written some of them in the Gate of Torah, God willing, so that hearts may long for Torah; and those who lack the capacity to study should at least know the splendor and honor of occupying oneself with it, and merit through this knowledge, so that their soul not be lost from the World to Come.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:157: And likewise included among heretics is one who calls his teacher by his own name. And they said that the reason Gehazi was punished was because he called his teacher by name, as it is said (II Kings 8:5), "This is the woman, and this is her son, whom Elisha restored to life."
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:158: And behold, the essence of all the punishments mentioned at this level is because of the desecration of the Torah. And our Sages of blessed memory said that the iniquity of desecrating the Name is greater than all other transgressions, and it cannot be atoned through teshuvah and suffering, as will be explained in the Gate of the Distinctions of Atonement. And our Sages of blessed memory said: retribution for the desecration of the Name is not delayed, whether it was inadvertent or deliberate. Now stand and consider the greatness of our obligation to sanctify the Name, for the essential purpose for which the Blessed Name sanctified us through His Torah and His commandments, and set us apart to be for Him [a people], was so that we sanctify Him and fear Him — for it is fitting that those who sanctify Him be holy, since even the vessels that serve before the Blessed Name must be holy, as it is said (Leviticus 22:32), "and you shall not profane My holy name, but I will be sanctified among the children of Israel; I am the Lord who sanctifies you." Set your heart to understand that the matter we have said is explained in this very verse. And it is said (Psalms 111:9), "He has commanded His covenant forever; holy and awesome is His name." Its meaning: because His name is holy and awesome, He commanded His covenant forever, and sanctified us through His commandments to sanctify Him and to fear Him. Therefore it is written immediately after (Psalms 111:10), "The beginning of wisdom is the fear of the Lord; good understanding, etc." And through the holiness of the commandments we are reckoned, in sanctifying the Blessed Name, together with the holy beings on high who sanctify and revere Him, as it is said (Psalms 89:8), "A God greatly revered in the council of the holy ones, etc."
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:159: There are further factions who have no share in the World to Come: the faction of the enemies of the Blessed Name, the faction of those who ravage the vineyard of the Name, and the faction of those who spread their terror in the land of the living. Behold, we shall set forth their matter, and the proofs of their punishment are explicit in the Torah. For the faction of the enemies of the Name shall perish from the World to Come, as it is said (Deuteronomy 7:10), "and repays those who hate Him to their face, to destroy them; He will not delay for one who hates Him, He will repay him to his face." Its meaning: He repays His enemies the reward of the commandments they perform in this world, so as to destroy them from the World to Come — and its Targum renders: "and He repays those who hate Him the good things which they perform before Him in their lifetime, to destroy them." And David said (Psalms 37:20), "For the wicked shall perish, and the enemies of the Lord shall be as the glory of the pastures; they shall vanish, in smoke they shall vanish." It mentions concerning the wicked the term "perish," which can refer to distress and exile, in the sense of what is said (Isaiah 27:13), "those who were lost in the land of Assyria, and the outcasts, etc.", (Jeremiah 50:6), "My people have been lost sheep", (Psalms 119:176), "I have gone astray like a lost sheep" — and it can also refer to death, in the sense of what is said (Psalms 31:13[?]), "then I perished in my affliction", (Esther 8:6), "in the loss of my kindred", (Leviticus 23:30), "and I will destroy that soul" — meaning excision from this world. For the wicked are punished with troubles and sufferings, or with death; and likewise they are punished by judgment for their deeds in the World to Come, at a fixed end and time. But the enemies of the Lord are compared to the fat of lambs and their suet, which is melted in fire and consumed in smoke — not compared to the flesh of the lambs, which becomes an ember with ash remaining. Therefore it says "in smoke they shall vanish, they shall vanish": just as the fat of lambs is consumed in smoke, so shall the enemies of the Name be consumed, for their soul shall be consumed and lost from the World to Come. And it is said (Exodus 20:5), "visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, upon the third and upon the fourth generation, [of those who hate Me]."
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:160: And the matter of enemies of the Name is sometimes found even among people who perform the commandments and are careful about every transgression in deed and in speech — if their soul is evil, and it is hard for them within their heart when their fellows occupy themselves with Torah, and it seems bad in their eyes when people serve the Lord and fear Him. This is like a man who does not wish that people honor and serve the king — for he is an enemy of the king; how much more so if they carry out their intent in deed, deterring people's hearts from the occupation with Torah and from the commandments, for they are enemies of the Lord. And likewise people who are stingy-eyed regarding the honor of upright and righteous Torah scholars, and hate the crown of their glory, or whose heart is grieved should the leadership of the generation come to them; and so it is written (I Samuel 8:7), "for they have not rejected you, but they have rejected Me, from reigning over them." And how much more so if they seek to turn their honor into shame or to lower them. And likewise if they love the honor of the wicked and their dominion over the dust — for these are truly enemies of the Name, and their will is not for the purity of His service, nor do they desire the sacred splendor of His fear and that His servants and those who fear Him increase greatly.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:161: And likewise the faction of those who ravage the vineyard of the Lord, such as informers and those who cause the multitude to sin — behold, they are enemies of the Name, just as you would say of men who destroy the king's cities, or his vineyards and orchards, that they are enemies of the king. And it is said (Isaiah 5:7), "For the vineyard of the Lord of hosts is the house of Israel, and the men of Judah His pleasant planting." And it is said (Psalms 83:4), "They take crafty counsel against Your people, and consult together against Your treasured ones," and it is said (Psalms 83:6), "For they have consulted together with one heart, against You they make a covenant," and it is said (Psalms 2:2), "and the rulers take counsel together against the Lord and against His anointed." Therefore our Sages of blessed memory said that those who sinned and caused the multitude to sin descend to Gehinnom and are judged there for generations upon generations.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:162: And concerning the faction of those who spread their terror in the land of the living, Ezekiel, peace upon him, spoke (Ezekiel 32:24), "who spread their terror in the land of the living, etc., and their iniquities were upon their bones." From this we learn that death does not atone for them, but rather their iniquities remain upon their bones forever. And our Sages of blessed memory said: the heretics, the apostates, the unbelievers, the informers, those who deny the Torah, those who deny the resurrection of the dead, those who separate themselves from the ways of the community, and those who spread their terror in the land of the living — such as communal leaders who cast excessive dread upon the community not for the sake of Heaven — and those who sinned and caused the multitude to sin, such as Jeroboam ben Nevat and his companions, descend to Gehinnom and are judged there for generations upon generations, as it is said (Isaiah 66:24), "And they shall go forth and look upon the corpses of the men who transgressed against Me, for their worm shall not die, etc."
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:163: And the punishment for those who spread their terror in the land of the living has five aspects: two on his own account, and three on account of the people. The two on his own account: the first, that man is a worm and a maggot, and is called such even while he is yet alive; and it is not enough for him not to bow down and lower himself, but he must exercise dominion, and exercise that dominion not for the sake of Heaven — and even by the mere thought of pride, without exercising actual dominion, a man is already corrupted, as it is said (Proverbs 16:5), "An abomination to the Lord is every proud heart."
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:164: And the second: a man is obligated to prepare the arrangement of his heart at all times, to establish within his heart dread and fear before the Blessed Name; and of the wicked it is said (Jeremiah 5:24), "neither do they say in their heart, Let us now fear the Lord our God." And the man who spreads his terror in the land of the living not for the sake of Heaven has no dread of the Name in his heart, yet wishes to cast his own dread upon His creatures; and instead of devising thoughts to establish the dread of the Name in his heart, he devises them to cast the dread of himself upon the people of the Blessed Name. And it is said (II Samuel 23:3), "He who rules over men righteously, ruling in the fear of God." Its meaning: it is fitting that a righteous man, who rules the fear of God [within himself], should rule over men — for since he fears the Blessed Name, it is fitting that his people should fear before him.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:165: And the three aspects on account of the people: the first, that he distresses the community by casting his dread upon them, and it is said (Leviticus 25:17), "You shall not wrong one another" — this concerns the matter of distress through words, as we have already explained.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:166: And the second: many stumbling-blocks come about through the casting of dread, as our Sages of blessed memory said: a man should never cast excessive dread within his own household, for behold, the concubine at Gibeah — her husband cast excessive dread upon her, and this brought down many myriads of Israel.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:167: And the third: the holy people, who are servants of the Blessed Name, ought not submit to flesh and blood, and it is not fitting that the dread of flesh and blood be upon them except for the sake of Heaven, as it is said (Leviticus 25:55), "For the children of Israel are servants to Me; they are My servants, and not servants to servants." And it is said (Exodus 19:6), "And you shall be to Me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation" — the term "priests" (kohanim) here meaning masters and princes, as likewise (II Samuel 8:18), "and David's sons were priests (kohanim)" [i.e., chief officials]. And all the people are called a "kingdom" (mamlachah), in the sense of (I Kings 18:10), "if there be any nation or kingdom," (Isaiah 60:12), "for the nation and the kingdom." Its meaning: you shall be to Me a kingdom entirely of princes, so that the yoke of flesh and blood not be upon you. And it is said (Isaiah 51:12), "Who are you, that you should be afraid of a man that shall die?" and it is said (Isaiah 51:7), "Fear not the reproach of men." And our Sages of blessed memory said: since those who call evil good and good evil have multiplied, the yoke of Heaven has been cast off from them, and the yoke of flesh and blood has been thrown upon them. And David the king, peace upon him, said (Psalms 9:20-21), "Arise, O Lord, let not man prevail; let the nations be judged before You. Put fear on them, O Lord, that the nations may know themselves to be but men, selah." From this we learn that at the time when man prevails, he does not recognize that he is merely man, for no dominion befits man except for the sake of Heaven.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:168: Now let us explain the matter of the punishment of those who separate themselves from the ways of the community, and that it is included among the punishments of the factions we have already stated. When the heads of the people and the holy congregations gather together to serve the Blessed Name, and agree upon resolutions to establish a commandment for themselves, behold, they sanctify the Name, may it be exalted and sanctified — as it is said (Deuteronomy 33:5), "And there was a king in Jeshurun, when the heads of the people were gathered, the tribes of Israel together." And it is said (Psalms 47:10), "The princes of the peoples are gathered together, the people of the God of Abraham, for the shields of the earth belong to God; He is greatly exalted." Israel are called "peoples" because they are twelve tribes, in the sense of (Deuteronomy 33:19), "They shall call peoples to the mountain" — yet they are one people to serve the Name; therefore it says "the people of the God of Abraham." And kings and princes are called "shields," in the sense of (Isaiah 21:5), "anoint the shield." Its meaning: the princes of the peoples are gathered to serve the exalted Name, for their kings and their princes belong to God, being His servants and His faithful ones, in the sense of what is said (Psalms 89:19), "For our shield belongs to the Lord, and our king to the Holy One of Israel." "He is greatly exalted" — for the Holy One, blessed be He, is exalted and glorified in His world through their gathering and their service. And the man who separates himself from the ways of the community is like one who accuses the resolution to serve the Lord, and like one who removes himself from the company of those who sanctify the Name, showing himself unwilling to be in their council and to be inscribed with their inscription — behold, he desecrates the [divine] service, and is included among the factions we have mentioned who scorn the word of the Name and have no share in the World to Come. And the second reason: they deter the hearts of the weak-minded by their withdrawal from the ways of the community, and they are thus among those who cause the multitude to sin.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:169: Now let us explain the matter of the faction who forsake the Lord. It is said that they are people who bear no yoke of the fear of Heaven, and they fulfill the commandments merely as a commandment learned by rote. And when the inclination overpowers such a man, and a spirit passes over him and he transgresses and becomes guilty, he does not sigh or worry over his sin; he eats and wipes his mouth, and in his own eyes it is as though he did no wrong — as it is said (Psalms 36:2), "An oracle of transgression to the wicked man within my heart: there is no dread of God before his eyes."
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:170: And there are among that evil faction those for whom it is not enough that they have not clothed themselves in dread, having transgressed statute and testimony — but they praise and bless their own souls when they fulfill their desire, and these provoke and spurn before the Name, as it is said (Psalms 10:3), "For the wicked boasts of his soul's desire, and the greedy blesses himself, he spurns the Lord." And Isaiah, peace upon him, spoke of the destruction of that faction, as it is said (Isaiah 1:28), "And the destruction of transgressors and sinners shall be together, and those who forsake the Lord shall be consumed." He compared the rebels and sinners to a broken vessel that leaves a remnant, but said that those who forsake the Name shall be consumed, that they have no share in the World to Come, as it is said (Malachi 3:19), "which shall leave them neither root nor branch."
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:171: And the destruction of the factions mentioned applies at the time they have not done teshuvah; but if they have turned back from their evil ways, their soul is saved from destruction, as it is said (Jeremiah 3:22), "Return, backsliding children, I will heal your backslidings."
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:172: Explanation of the matters concerning the iniquities of the four factions: our Sages, of blessed memory, said that four factions do not receive the presence of the Divine Presence: the faction of scoffers, the faction of liars, the faction of flatterers, and the faction of those who speak evil speech. The faction of scoffers, as it is written (Hosea 7:5), "he stretched out his hand with scoffers." The faction of liars, as it is written (Psalms 101:7), "He who speaks lies shall not be established before my eyes." The faction of flatterers, as it is written (Job 13:16), "for a flatterer shall not come before Him." The faction of those who speak evil speech, as it is written (Psalms 5:5), "For You are not a God who desires wickedness; evil shall not sojourn with You."
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:173: Now let us give ear to the character of their matters and the nature of their ways, to grant you understanding of the choicest depths of these matters; and we shall divide them into their parts, and reveal in full the severity of the punishment for their loathsome deeds, and you shall gain much benefit through the arrangement of these parts. For perhaps, before you grasped our words, you had not weighed the true meaning of the weight of transgression in each of their parts, and had not beheld the harsh outlook and the severity of the punishment in each of them; perhaps you saw only a portion of it, but not the whole of it. And each part that we set out first is graver than the next. And through our words, even in the lighter parts that we shall mention, you will recognize the terrors of the shadow of death and know that their end is the ways of death; and perhaps until now your ears had not been opened, and they seemed to you like a straight path. But now that we write of their bitterness, bring their dread into your thoughts, and let it come also into the chambers of your spirit — the well-founded matters, when you see that I have brought forth for myself faithful witnesses: reason and the verses of Scripture, and the words of the Sages and their wondrous riddles — let them be for testimony and for a sign. And by this the truth shall be tested upon you, and a spirit of favor shall be poured upon you from on high, and you shall burn away the evil traits from within you, and clear words will support your heart.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:174: And this is the matter of the faction of scoffers. Scoffing is divided into five parts. The first part: a man of the tongue who casts blame upon people, as it is said (Psalms 50:20), "You sit and speak against your brother; you slander your own mother's son." And he is called a "scoffer" (letz), as it is said (Proverbs 21:24), "Proud, haughty, scoffer is his name, who deals in the fury of pride." Its meaning: two evil traits, presumption and pride, are gathered and joined together in the scoffing man; for without gaining any benefit from the matter, he causes tremendous harm to his fellows, making their reputation stink in people's eyes — and this is an extreme of presumption, greater even than the robber and the plunderer, who at least act to increase their own wealth. And he is also haughty, for the lowly and submissive man, when he recognizes his own deficiencies and flaws, does not mock other people. And our Sages of blessed memory said (Taanit 8a): in the time to come, all the animals will gather near the serpent and say to it, The lion tears prey and eats, the wolf preys and eats — you, what benefit do you gain [from your bite]? It answered them: And what benefit does the master of the tongue gain? — as it is said (Ecclesiastes 10:11), "If the serpent bites before it is charmed, then there is no advantage to the charmer" [i.e., master of the tongue]. And this part is also among the parts of the faction of those who speak evil speech.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:175: The second part — one who mocks people, scorning them in his heart for the shortness of their attainment in virtues, or in the successes of the time, in honor and authority, or scorning them for their poverty and want; and pride has brought him to this trait, or an abundance of ease and pleasure, as it is said (Psalms 123:4), "Our soul has had more than enough of the scorn of those at ease, of the contempt of the proud." And sometimes the scoffer mocks even the holy and the prophets, as it is said (Jeremiah 20:7), "the whole of it mocks me." And Solomon the king, peace upon him, said (Proverbs 14:21), "He who scorns his fellow sins." It is further said (ibid.), "He who scorns his fellow lacks a heart," and it is said (Proverbs 17:5), "He who mocks the poor blasphemes his Maker; he who rejoices at calamity shall not go unpunished." Its meaning: one who mocks the poor man shows by this that he believes success lies in people's own hands, and that they attain it through their own wisdom — in the sense of what is said (Deuteronomy 8:17), "and you say in your heart, My power and the might of my hand have gained me this wealth," and it is said (Isaiah 10:13), "For he said, By the strength of my hand I have done it, and by my wisdom, for I am prudent." And because of this, one who mocks the poor man — for he says in his heart that the poor man did not attain wealth because of his own lack of understanding and the weakness of his hands — behold, he thereby blasphemes the Maker of both the poor and the rich, for everything comes from the Blessed Name, in the sense of what is said (Proverbs 22:2), "The rich and the poor meet together; the Lord is the maker of them all." And of one who rejoices at calamity it says, "shall not go unpunished" — for even though he did not cause harm in deed or in speech, he shall not go unpunished; yet the evil of one who rejoices at calamity does not reach the evil of the mocker. And because scoffing arises from pride, which is the opposite of humility, Solomon the king, peace upon him, said (Proverbs 3:34), "Surely He scoffs at the scoffers, but gives grace to the humble." Its meaning: "surely" — truly, the scoffers who mock people — the Blessed Name shall scoff at them, in the sense of what is said (Psalms 2:4), "He who sits in the heavens shall laugh; the Lord shall have them in derision." And the word "surely" (im) serves to affirm the matter, as also in (Numbers 24:22), "surely (ki im) Kain shall be for burning," (Proverbs 23:18), "surely (ki im) there is a future."
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:176: The third part — one who continually mocks matters and actions, without intending to demean their doers, but distancing things that ought not be distanced, and distancing the benefit of actions whose benefit is still hoped for. Of this it is said (Proverbs 13:13), "He who scorns a matter will be pledged to it." And they said: do not scorn any man, and do not dismiss any matter, for there is no man who has not his hour, and no thing that has not its place. And this scoffer was brought to his evil trait by being wise in his own eyes; and sometimes this trait brings a man to heresy, to the point of mocking the commandments, as it is said (Psalms 119:51), "The proud have mocked me exceedingly; yet I have not turned aside from Your Torah." And this third part is the faction that does not accept rebuke, as it is said (Proverbs 9:8), "Rebuke not a scoffer, lest he hate you," and it is said (Proverbs 9:7), "He who corrects a scoffer gets himself shame," and it is said (Proverbs 19:25), "Strike a scoffer, and the simple will beware." And what leads this faction to refuse to hear ethical instruction is that the trait which brings about this scoffer is the trait of being wise in one's own eyes; and this trait rules him so completely that he comes to mock even the knowledge of another — and this is the trait for which there is no hope, as it is said (Proverbs 26:12), "Do you see a man wise in his own eyes? There is more hope for a fool than for him."
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:177:
The fourth part — one who fixes himself continually to idle talk and worthless words in the manner of those who sit at street corners. And there are two evils in this evil matter: the first, that whoever multiplies words brings about sin; and the second, that he is idle from words of Torah. And there is in this matter a path of death, for how has he not remembered and taken to heart that in those very times which he destroys, he could attain pleasantness and acquire eternal life, if he set aside those very appointed times for Torah, in which he is free from his work and his affairs? This is nothing but his heart demeaning the commandments and the reward of the World to Come. And beyond having lost much good, he shall bear his iniquity, for the guilt of idleness from Torah when one has the ability to occupy oneself with it is a fire that consumes unto destruction, as they said, "he has despised the word of the Lord" refers to whoever is able to occupy himself with Torah and does not do so, as we have already stated for you. And they said, of blessed memory: whoever goes to a place where an assembly has gathered for frivolity — this is the "seat of scoffers," and of him Scripture says (Psalms 1:1), "nor sat in the seat of scoffers," and it is written afterward, "but his delight is in the Torah of the Lord." You have learned from this that the seat of scoffers leads to the neglect of Torah. And whoever has not set his heart to occupy himself with Torah in his idle hours should at least take counsel for his own soul so that it not be lost, secluding himself in those hours to think of his end, to understand his latter days, to search his ways, and to acquire the virtues of the soul and draw near to the Blessed Name.
The fifth part — one who mocks with mere words of the lips concerning deeds and matters, not that he scorns them in his heart, but out of the manner of those who rejoice for no reason, not according to the proper measure of laughter. And sometimes this is brought about by the drinking of wine and drunkenness, as it is said (Proverbs 20:1), "Wine is a scoffer, strong drink is raging; and whoever errs because of it is not wise." Its meaning: the man of wine is a scoffer, the man of strong drink is raging, and whoever errs because of it is not wise — in the manner of (Psalms 109:4), "but I am prayer" [i.e., a man of prayer]. And its intent is that the drinking of wine brings about three evil things: the first, that the man becomes a scoffer; the second, that he becomes raging and full of words, as our Sages of blessed memory said, whoever multiplies words brings about sin, and it is said (Ecclesiastes 5:2), "and the voice of a fool comes with many words"; and the third, that "whoever errs because of it is not wise." And know that the practice of scoffing does not become fixed in a person's soul until he has cast off the yoke of Heaven from himself; therefore he is punished by bearing the yoke of suffering, measure for measure, as it is said (Isaiah 28:22), "Now therefore do not scoff, lest your bonds grow strong." And our Sages of blessed memory said: whoever scoffs, sufferings come upon him, as it is said, "lest your bonds grow strong." And the Sages would warn their disciples not to scoff even by way of chance and happenstance; and they needed to warn concerning this part especially, because many stumble in it by way of chance.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:178: And this is the matter of the faction of liars. The matter of this faction divides into nine parts. The first part — a man of falsehood who has forsaken the Torah, and does evil and destroys through the utterance of his mouth — such as one who denies his fellow regarding a deposit, a pledge in hand, or a hired laborer's wages, as it is said (Leviticus 19:11), "You shall not deal falsely, nor lie to one another." And likewise one who testifies falsely against his fellow, as it is said (Exodus 20:13), "You shall not answer against your fellow as a false witness." And this part includes deceit and fraud in trade and partnership, and it is said (Leviticus 25:14), "You shall not wrong one another," and it is said (Psalms 55:12), "nor does deceit and guile depart from her open square." He is called "a man of iniquity" and "belial," and is heavy with iniquity among the factions of the wicked, as we have already stated in the Gates of the Fear of Sin. And the traits of this man of iniquity are that he winks with his eyes and speaks with his fingers, as it is said (Proverbs 6:12-13), "A man of belial, a man of iniquity... winks with his eyes, etc."
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:179: The second part — one who lies where there is no actual damage or loss to his fellow in the essence of the lie itself, but where it is possible that it become a cause of damage and evil — such as one who deceives his fellow into believing that he is a loving and faithful friend to him, intending by this that the other trust him and not guard himself from him, so that he may bring evil upon him. Of this it is said (Jeremiah 9:7-8), "With his mouth he speaks peace to his fellow, but in his heart he lays his ambush," and it is said afterward, "Shall I not punish them for these things, says the Lord? Shall My soul not be avenged on such a nation as this?" And the punishment for these two parts is for two matters: for the lie itself and for the harm bound up in its folds; for the lie itself, besides the aspect of harm, is an abomination to the Lord, as it is said (Proverbs 6:16-18), "These six things the Lord hates, etc., a proud look, a lying tongue, etc., a heart that devises wicked thoughts." And it is said (Proverbs 8:13), "and a perverse mouth I hate," and it is said (Job 15:16), "how much more one who is abominable and corrupt, a man who drinks iniquity like water." And even flesh and blood find falsehood loathsome, as it is said (Proverbs 12:22), "Lying lips are an abomination to the Lord."
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:180: The third part — one who comes with cunning and deceptive words to withhold good from its rightful owner in order to transfer it to himself — not to rob or steal directly from his fellow something that is his, but to set his eye on some benefit that is about to come to his fellow, and lie in wait for it to take it for himself, through the falsehood of his words; or he devises through his lies to have his fellow give him a gift. The primary punishment is for the lie; yet the punishment for the lie grows greater when it brings about loss to another, even though the essential punishment is not for the loss itself, since the other did not lose something he had already acquired — in the manner of what our Sages of blessed memory said: whoever alters his speech is as though he worshipped idols, as it is said (Genesis 27:12), "Perhaps my father will feel me, and I shall be in his eyes as a deceiver," and it is said concerning idolatry (Jeremiah 10:15), "they are vanity, a work of mockery." And our Sages of blessed memory said "as though he worshipped idols," bringing the comparison for one aspect: that he is hidden within falsehood and helped along by vanity.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:181: The fourth part — one who lies in relating things he has heard, deliberately altering some of them, gaining no benefit from his lies nor causing loss to another; but his practice stems from his love of falsehood, "speaking righteousness, selah" being far from him. And sometimes he fabricates the entire account from his own mind. This man's punishment is lighter in one respect, since no man suffers loss from his lies and recklessness; but his punishment is very great for his brazenness and his love of falsehood, and his iniquity grows heavy since he loves it without benefit. And Solomon the king, peace upon him, said (Proverbs 6:19), "a false witness who breathes out lies." Its meaning: if you see a man who breathes out lies in his conversation and the relating of his affairs, know that this trait will bring him to testify falsely against his brother and to speak perversely of him, out of his love of falsehood. And this part they permitted for the fulfillment of a commandment and the pursuit of good and peace; and they said it is permitted to praise the bride before the groom and to say she is comely and graceful even if this is not so. And they said it is permitted to alter one's words for the sake of peace, as it is said (Genesis 50:16-17), "Your father commanded before his death, saying, So shall you say to Joseph, Forgive, I pray you, etc." And there are people who alter some of the things they heard unknowingly, because they did not take care to examine them carefully when they heard them; this too is an evil trait. And Solomon the king, peace upon him, said (Proverbs 21:28), "but the man who listens will speak forever." Its meaning: a man who sets his heart to listen and give ear to the true nature of the things spoken in his ears, in order to relate them accurately, and in whose mouth is found no tongue of deceit, will speak forever — for people will love to hear his words, and will never say to him, Why do you speak your words further?
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:182: The fifth part — one who tells his fellow that he will do him good and give him a gift, and while he is still speaking, converses within his own heart that he will not give it. And it is said (Psalms 34:14), "Keep your tongue from evil, and your lips from speaking deceit." Our Sages of blessed memory explained (Bava Metzia 49a) that one should not speak one thing with the mouth and another with the heart. They further said there are matters that carry the taint of "lacking faithfulness" if one goes back on them, provided that what he says with his mouth he has firmly resolved in his mind.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:183: The sixth part — one who promises his fellow to do him good, and then falsifies his words and nullifies his statement; for since he has said he would do him good, by way of promise, and his fellow's heart trusted him, he has no right to violate his promise, for this is a way of falsehood, and he is like a man who has broken a covenant, as it is said (Zephaniah 3:13), "The remnant of Israel shall not do iniquity, nor speak lies, nor shall a deceitful tongue be found in their mouth." And likewise one who says he will give his fellow a small gift, even though he did not use the language of promise — our Sages said this too carries the taint of "lacking faithfulness," for his fellow's heart relies and trusts in him, since the gift is small, that he will surely give it. And if he is a poor man, even though the gift is large, if he goes back on it, his wrongdoing is great, for he has made a vow, and it is said (Numbers 30:3), "he shall not break his word." And likewise one who boasts before many people that he will give a gift to someone — behold, he is thereby glorying in his own generosity, and this is like a promise, and it is not proper for him to retract his words after having gained honor and glory through the matter — in the manner of what is written (Proverbs 25:14), "Like clouds and wind without rain is a man who boasts of a false gift." Its meaning: just as people become distressed after the signs of rain appear and the rain does not come, so is the matter of a man who boasts of a false gift — for his very boasting about the matter is a sign that the matter will be fulfilled; therefore the man he promised the gift to becomes distressed when his hope is disappointed.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:184: The seventh part — one who deceives his fellow into thinking that he did him a favor or spoke well of him, when he did not. Our Sages of blessed memory said it is forbidden to steal people's minds. And behold, this sin is graver among the Sages of Israel than robbery, because a lying tongue carries great guilt, and we have been obligated in the fences of truth, for it is among the foundations of the soul.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:185: The eighth part — one who boasts of virtues not found in him. Solomon the king, peace upon him, said (Proverbs 17:7), "Excellent speech is not fitting for a fool; how much less lying speech for a noble man." Its meaning: it is not fitting for a fool to be proud and exalt himself over the virtue of his ancestors, for it is said in the verse just before (Proverbs 17:6), "and the glory of children is their fathers" — how much less is it fitting for a noble man to glorify himself with falsehood, saying, Thus I did, and I distributed and gave, when he did no such thing. This is a disgrace for any man, and all the more so for a noble one, and it disparages the acts of charity he actually performed, for he has profaned his own soul over what he did not do — for this will testify that his heart, in all the acts of righteousness he performed, sought only name and praise. And our Sages of blessed memory said that one who is honored with degrees of honor fitting for someone who knows two tractates, when he knows only one, should say to them, I know only the one alone. How much more so is it forbidden to lie and boast, saying, We have heard many such things.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:186: The ninth part — children who do not lie in relating things they have heard or reporting events, but alter matters concerning their own wishes where no loss to any person is involved, yet find almost a pleasure in their lying even though they gain no money by it. Our Sages said that this too is forbidden, as it is said (Jeremiah 9:4[5]), "they have taught their tongue to speak lies." But their punishment is not like the punishment of those who lie for no reason at all, whose matter we mentioned in the fifth part (read: the fourth). Behold, these are the parts of the faction of liars; and we have already stated for you earlier the foundations in the ways of a man of faithfulness, and that they are foundations of the soul.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:187: And this is the matter of the faction of flatterers. The matter of this faction divides into nine parts. The first part — the flatterer who recognized, or saw, or knew that there is iniquity in his fellow's hand, and that he has taken hold of deceit, or that one man sinned against another through evil speech or wronging through words, and yet he smooths his tongue for him, saying, You have done no wrong. How much smaller is the iniquity of one who merely refrains from rebuke, as it is said (Leviticus 19:17), "You shall surely rebuke your fellow, and not bear sin because of him" — and he continues to sin by his very saying, You have not sinned, in the sense of what is said (Jeremiah 23:14), "and they strengthen the hands of evildoers." And behold, this is, at the hand of the foolish flatterer, a criminal iniquity, for he is not zealous for the truth, but helps along the falsehood, calling evil good, and turning darkness into light. He has also placed a stumbling-block before the sinner in two respects: the first, that the sinner does not repent of his evil; and the second, that he will repeat his folly on the morrow — for the wicked man was praised by the flatterer for the desire of his own soul. Besides this, he shall bear punishment for the harm he did to the one whom the sinner wronged, by justifying before him the one who sinned against him — besides being punished for the matter of falsehood, as it is said (Psalms 5:7), "You shall destroy those who speak lies," and it is said (Proverbs 17:15), "He who justifies the wicked, and he who condemns the righteous, both alike are an abomination to the Lord." How much more so if the wrong in the hand of his fellow the wicked man is known publicly, for by saying to him before people, You are pure, without transgression, he has desecrated and demeaned law and justice.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:188: And a man is obligated to expose himself to danger and not bring upon his soul such a guilty iniquity. And our Sages said concerning the matter of Agrippa, who was reading in the Torah, and when he reached this verse (Deuteronomy 17:15), "You may not put a foreign man over you," his eyes streamed with tears, and they said to him, You are our brother! At that moment the enemies of Israel became liable to destruction, for they had flattered Agrippa. How much more so should one who sits in judgment have no fear of a man who shall die, as it is said (Deuteronomy 1:17), "You shall not be afraid of the face of any man." And this part which we have mentioned is the part of a wicked man who is counted among two evil factions, from his joining together falsehood and flattery. And there are further parts within the faction of flatterers in which the flatterer is destroyed and lost through the iniquity of flattery alone, as will be explained.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:189: The second part — the flatterer who praises a wicked man before people, whether in his presence or not in his presence — even though he does not justify him in his violence or lie concerning his judgment, but merely says of him that he is a good man. Of this it is said (Proverbs 28:4), "Those who forsake the Torah praise the wicked." For had he not forsaken the Torah, he would not have praised one who transgresses its words and breaks its commandments. And even if he does not praise the wicked man except for whatever good is found in him, and speaks of him before people so as to declare the man's uprightness — this too is a grievous evil, for in remembering the good he does not remember the evil, and he covers over all his transgressions; he will be reckoned righteous among his listeners, and they will give him honor and lift up his hand, and he will grow strong. And we have already made known to you the stumbling-blocks and corruptions found in honoring the wicked. Therefore it is not proper to mention their righteousness unless one also mentions their wickedness and their folly, as it is said (Proverbs 10:7), "but the name of the wicked shall rot," and it is said (Isaiah 57:12), "I will declare your righteousness, and your works, but they shall not profit you." Its meaning: good deeds shall not profit you to save you from your evil, when I arise for judgment and weigh against them the abundance of your transgressions and your deeds of mockery, for your words of iniquity outweigh them. And as our Sages said, whoever has more iniquities than merits is inscribed and sealed for death. And the wicked are recognizable by their conversation and their conduct, as we have already stated for you in the Gates of the Fear of Sin.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:190: And behold, the righteous find the wicked man loathsome, as it is said (Proverbs 29:27), "An abomination to the righteous is a man of iniquity." And one who is not in the council of the righteous — if he loathes, he does not truly loathe him; if he curses, he does not truly curse him; and if he blesses, he does not truly bless him.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:191: And it is possible that the case of one who praises the wicked man arises, by chance, from mere naivete — for the naive man thinks to praise good is good, if it were true, and if it were his actual due. And unknowingly, he praises the dead — for our Sages said, concerning the wicked, that they are reckoned as departed spirits (refaim) even while alive, and are called dead, as it is said (Ecclesiastes 9:5), "but the dead know nothing." And this error amounts to a deliberate transgression, for a servant ought not love his master if he loves those who hate him and draws near those far from him — is it not for him to know, through the very way of knowledge, that this is so? And it is said (Proverbs 3:35), "but fools carry off shame" — and we have already explained its meaning.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:192: The third part — the flatterer who praises the wicked man to his face; even his own wisdom stood by him not to praise him before other people, lest it become a snare to them — yet this too is a flatterer whose iniquity is great, for he has flattered him regarding himself, so that he will not turn back from his evil way nor worry over his iniquities, since he is righteous in his own eyes. And of anyone who is not of the company of the righteous, if they praise him, he will say in his heart, Indeed, I knew this to be so. In the sense of what is said (ibid. v. 11 [Proverbs 29:5]), "A man who flatters his fellow with his mouth spreads a net for his feet" [alternate rendering used here: destroys his fellow], "but the righteous shall be delivered through knowledge." Its meaning: the flatterer destroys his fellow with his mouth, for he praises him and the other believes his words and hardens his spirit, regarding his own soul as precious, and does not understand that his soul is corrupted, this stumbling-block being at his own hand; his heart also grows haughty, and he falls into the snares of his own pride. And behold, he was truly destroyed through the flattery of the [flatterer's] lips — "but the righteous shall be delivered through knowledge" — the righteous shall be delivered, through their own knowledge, from the harms of the flatterer, for even if he should praise them, their heart will not grow haughty because of it, in the manner of what our Sages said: even if the whole world says of you, You are righteous, regard yourself as wicked. And they said, If you have friends, some of whom praise you and some of whom rebuke you, love those who rebuke you and hate those who praise you, for the former bring you to eternal life, while the latter make you rejoice in your own harm by praising you. And it is also possible to explain "but the righteous shall be delivered through knowledge" as referring to their companions — that they will not flatter them, but rebuke them and guide them on the way when they stray into a trackless void. And it is said (Proverbs 26:28), "and a smooth mouth works ruin" — it compares a smooth mouth to a slippery path, saying that just as a man falls and is thrust down as he walks on a slippery path — as it is said (Psalms 35:5-6), "Let them be as chaff, etc., and let the angel of the Lord thrust them down; let their way be dark and slippery" — so does a man fall and get thrust down by a smooth mouth, and this is the flatterer's mouth. And concerning the matter we have explained, David the king, peace upon him, said (Psalms 12:4), "May the Lord cut off all flattering lips, the tongue that speaks great things." He cursed the smooth mouth for it destroys its fellow through it — and the harsh tongue, which is the opposite of the smooth, is evil speech. And there are among the flatterers those who intend to flatter men of power so that these will honor and exalt them; and our Sages said, whoever flatters his fellow for the sake of honor will in the end be repaid with shame.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:193: The fourth part — one who associates with a wicked man; and it is not enough that he fails to rebuke him with the staff of his mouth and keep him at a distance, but he draws him near like a friend. And it is said (II Chronicles 20:37), "Because you have joined yourself, etc., the Lord has broken your works." And the righteous utterly despise the wicked man, as it is said (Psalms 15:4), "in whose eyes a vile person is despised." And our Sages of blessed memory said (Bava Kamma 92b): the starling does not go to the crow for nothing, but because it is of its kind. And they said (Ben Sira 13:14[?]): every bird dwells with its own kind, and man with his like. And they said (Megillah 28a): it is forbidden to gaze upon the image of a wicked man, as it is said (II Kings 3:14), "Were it not that I regard the presence of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, I would not look toward you, nor see you." And they said, whoever gazes upon the image of a wicked man, his eyes grow dim in his old age — as it is said (Genesis 27:1), "And it came to pass, when Isaac was old, that his eyes grew dim so that he could not see," because he had gazed upon the image of Esau, even though he did not recognize his deeds, since Esau concealed his actions, in the sense of what is said, "their works were in the dark." And we have already made known to you clearly earlier how many are the ways of death found for one who associates with a wicked man.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:194: The fifth part — a man in whom people believe, and all who hear him rely upon his words, and who intends to elevate one of the people, or a relative close to him whom he loves, and says of him that he is a wise man, when he is not a wise man at all — this becomes a stumbling-block and a rock of offense, for people will rely upon his rulings, and every dispute will be decided by his word, and he will pervert judgment and bring ruin upon the world. And likewise if he says of a man that he is trustworthy in spirit, without having verified whether he is truly a man of faithfulness, when he is not to be trusted at all — and perhaps the one who hears will appoint him over his household and place all his possessions in his hand, and the man will deny it, saying, I never saw you. And our Sages said (Sanhedrin 7b): whoever appoints a judge who is unfit is as though he planted a sacred tree (asherah); and if it is done in a place where a Torah scholar was fit to serve, it is as though he planted it beside the altar. And there was one who, in earlier days, set up as head someone unfit to render halachic rulings, and they applied to him the verse (Habakkuk 2:19), "Woe to him who says to the wood, Awake; to the dumb stone, Arise; it shall teach! Behold, it is overlaid with gold and silver, yet there is no breath at all within it." And the Holy One, blessed be He, is destined to exact retribution from those who appoint such men, as it is said (Habakkuk 2:20), "But the Lord is in His holy palace; let all the earth be silent before Him."
